heading: Tac: eight service languages
body: Tac supports shared role modules in JavaScript, TypeScript, Dart, Swift, Kotlin, C#, Rust and Go. The example declares a MoneyEntity mapping in the required client/entities folder. Table is a modifier and does not change that path. The view shows local service state, not the result of a database query. Declaring an entity does not connect to a database and does not fetch data. To run queries, explicitly supply an authorized public client adapter and own its behavior context. Select one language tab and copy its service file and entity file. The shared page client/pages/tac.html places <money-panel hydrate="load" />, and the view reads {money.amount}. Annotation discovery selects that language automatically. The native application opens that page, because the manifest's start_url is /. JavaScript, TypeScript and Dart run on every target. Rust links on macOS, Windows and Linux, C# links on Windows, and both reach every other target, including the web, as WebAssembly. Go reaches every target as WebAssembly (ADR 0035, ADR 0037, ADR 0045). Swift runs only on Apple platforms and Kotlin only on Android. So a Swift or Kotlin service needs a browser sibling for the web. Keep the native MoneyService type first in the file. The compiler appends the discovered entity declarations after it. Tac stays client-rendered. It uses only public TAC_ configuration, never private Yon credentials.
